project.visitorDecision: Choose whether to follow a near-term AIS-supported Canal Park passage or independently published later arrivals, then select a camera or public shoreline view.
project.primaryAction: Open the next supported vessel on the live map, inspect the camera, or check later traffic in the separate published harbor forecast.

claims.subject: other
claims.limitation: The AIS engine publishes only qualified near-term candidate passage windows; it does not prove bridge opening or all scheduled harbor traffic.

claims.subject: other
claims.limitation: An independently published arrival or departure forecast is not confirmation a particular vessel will pass Canal Park or that it will pass at that time.

claims.subject: other
claims.limitation: The operator's listed camera feeds do not guarantee an active stream, a specific camera angle, or vessel passage.

decisionState.selectedIdField: data.watchPick.mmsi, or no selected vessel when AIS evidence is insufficient
decisionState.sourceOfTruth: Existing /api/duluth-canal AIS candidate decision; independent Harbor Lookout link is never promoted into AIS evidence.
decisionState.unavailableBehavior: When AIS fails or there is no candidate, keep the independent published schedule and direct camera operator links visible; a missing map falls back to readable shore viewing cards.

scenarios.input: Fresh AIS returns one qualified arrival candidate
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: The named vessel and evidence-bounded passage window appear first with map, camera and shore choice actions.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Do not call the vessel ETA official or guarantee bridge opening.

scenarios.input: Fresh AIS returns no qualified next watch
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Explicit no-supported-passage message remains beside a link to later published harbor arrivals and departures.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: No candidate is not interpreted as zero harbor traffic.

scenarios.input: Select shore locations, camera, then return to next vessel
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Existing monitor controls can return from shore and camera views to the selected vessel if AIS remains current.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Existing map interaction should retain source age and cannot invent a fresh candidate.

scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Published harbor forecast and operator camera links remain available in regular HTML.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: No fabricated live timing appears without running the AIS client.

scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Choose a shore view scrolls to the readable North Side, Park Point and Lakewalk descriptions.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: A shore-card description is not a verified parking entrance or live bridge condition.

scenarios.input: AIS request fails after first successful response
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Existing retained-data warning remains; the independent published schedule never becomes a supported passage.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Previous AIS positions are not passed off as refreshed live traffic.

failures.no-js: Keep the independent Harbor Lookout forecast link and direct camera publisher link in static HTML with a clear notice that live AIS requires JavaScript.
failures.no-tiles: Expose readable shore-view choices and official visitor-center details even when Leaflet or basemap tiles do not render.
failures.no-image: Keep the vessel decision and source links without depending on the existing credited Great Lakes freighter photograph.
failures.stale-data: Retain explicit failed-refresh status and never create a new supported passage from an expired AIS report.

qa.scopeNote: Source and structural tests are added; actual 390/1280 before-after screenshots, keyboard and media/map browser checks have not been captured.
